I've been using a smart lock on my front door for five or six years now, and I've tried quite a few models. For most people, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice — it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a wide variety of unlocking methods. Whether you prefer fingerprint or keypad entry, it's got you covered.

HomeKit Weekly is a column series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ says the Bolt Fingerprint is its first smart lock to offer full Apple Home integration, and honestly, that's exactly what drew me in. I still miss Touch ID on my iPhone to this day. You can lock or unlock through the Home app or Siri, and if you've set up a HomePod or Apple TV as a home hub, you can include it in automations and scenes just like any other Apple Home accessory — and control it from anywhere.

However, I did notice one thing missing for me: Home Key support. If I could just tap my iPhone or Apple Watch to open the door, this lock would be perfect. That's the one area where it falls short, but it's not a dealbreaker.

I'm hoping ULTRALOQ adds this feature in the next generation, because once it supports Home Key, this lock will go from good to nearly perfect. It's also compatible with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, so no matter which smart home platform you prefer — or even if you switch down the road — you're covered. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi instead of Bluetooth, so basic remote control through its app doesn't require an additional bridge.

More unlocking methods than you'll ever use

The unlocking options on the Bolt Fingerprint are genuinely impressive. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingerprints along with 50 codes. You can unlock via the mobile app, auto-unlock as you approach the door, or use voice control through Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. Two physical keys are included in the box, so even if the battery dies, you'll never get locked out. For me, a smart lock without a physical key as backup isn't even worth considering.

You can set up to 50 custom codes, and you can also generate one-time or time-limited codes for friends, guests, or your cleaning lady. If you rent out your place, this feature alone is worth the price of admission.

It also has a Lockout mode that temporarily disables all electronic access, including codes and app access. For anyone about to go on a trip and wanting extra peace of mind while the house is empty, this feature is genuinely useful. I never would have thought a smart lock would have this, but it's a nice bonus.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I've installed more smart locks over the past few years than I can count, so for me the process is second nature. As long as you have the right tools handy, it takes about ten minutes. If you're replacing an existing deadbolt, there's no wiring or drilling required. All you need is a Phillips screwdriver, though it's worth replacing the strike plate on the door frame while you're at it.

Once you scan the lock into Apple Home setup and assign it to a room, you can control it through the Home app, or add it to automations and scenes that trigger multiple actions at once — like the lights turning on the moment the door unlocks.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint wrap-up

All in all, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a really solid choice. In day-to-day use, fingerprint unlock quickly becomes your go-to method. Installation is straightforward too. I've had it on my office door for a while now because I often have laptops sitting around waiting to be shipped out, and I wanted an extra layer of security. I love that it auto-unlocks as I approach, and I can also see who's come and gone. The fingerprint recognition brings me right back to the days of Touch ID.

You can pick up the Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ website.
